name: isUndefined
summary: Checks whether a value is exactly `undefined`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is `undefined`; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check to distinguish `undefined` from `null` and other empty-looking values. It does not convert the input.

name: isNull
summary: Checks whether a value is exactly `null`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is `null`; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check when `null` has a different meaning from `undefined`. To accept both, use `isNullish`.

name: isBoolean
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive boolean or a genuine boxed `Boolean`.
notes:
Uses the built-in wrapper operation to read the stored value. Overridden `valueOf` methods and `Symbol.toStringTag` properties are ignored; prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers return `false`.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`: a structural wrapper interface does not prove native identity. For primitive-only narrowing, use an exact name such as `"boolean"`, `"number"` or `"string"` with `isTypeOf`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive boolean or genuine boxed `Boolean`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts both primitive boolean values and wrapper objects such as `new Boolean(false)`, including wrappers from another realm. It checks the stored native value without converting other inputs.
tooltip: Accepts wrappers from another realm, but rejects prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers. Does not invoke overridden conversion methods.

name: isNumber
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive number or a genuine boxed `Number`.
notes:
Uses the built-in wrapper operation to read the stored value. Overridden `valueOf` methods and `Symbol.toStringTag` properties are ignored; prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers return `false`.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`: a structural wrapper interface does not prove native identity. For primitive-only narrowing, use an exact name such as `"boolean"`, `"number"` or `"string"` with `isTypeOf`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive number or genuine boxed `Number`, including `NaN` and infinities; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts both primitive number values and wrapper objects such as `new Number(42)`, including wrappers from another realm. It checks the stored native value without converting other inputs. `NaN` and positive or negative infinity are numbers for this check.
tooltip: Accepts wrappers from another realm, but rejects prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers. Does not invoke overridden conversion methods. Includes `NaN` and infinities.

name: isString
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive string or a genuine boxed `String`.
notes:
Uses the built-in wrapper operation to read the stored value. Overridden `valueOf` methods and `Symbol.toStringTag` properties are ignored; prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers return `false`.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`: a structural wrapper interface does not prove native identity. For primitive-only narrowing, use an exact name such as `"boolean"`, `"number"` or `"string"` with `isTypeOf`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive string or genuine boxed `String`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts both primitive string values and wrapper objects such as `new String('hello')`, including wrappers from another realm. It checks the stored native value without converting other inputs.
tooltip: Accepts wrappers from another realm, but rejects prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers. Does not invoke overridden conversion methods.

name: isSymbol
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive symbol.
notes: Unlike `isBoolean`, `isNumber` and `isString`, this check does not accept a wrapper object. Use `toSymbol` to unbox a genuine Symbol wrapper when conversion is intended.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive symbol; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts symbols such as `Symbol("key")`. A boxed symbol, created with `Object(symbol)`, returns `false`.
tooltip: Boxed symbols return `false`.

name: isBigInt
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive bigint.
notes: Unlike `isBoolean`, `isNumber` and `isString`, this check does not accept a wrapper object. Strings and numbers are not converted; use `toBigInt` when conversion is intended.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive bigint; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts primitive bigint values without converting strings or numbers. A boxed bigint returns `false`.
tooltip: Boxed bigints return `false`; numeric strings are not converted.

name: isPrimitive
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive rather than an object or function.
notes: The browser object `document.all` returns `false`, even though its historical `typeof` result is `"undefined"`. The check uses the same object/function boundary as `isObject`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive, including `null` or `undefined`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts `null`, `undefined`, booleans, numbers, strings, bigints and symbols. Wrapper objects and functions return `false`. This is the complement of `isObject`, including for the browser object `document.all`.
tooltip: Includes `null` and `undefined`; rejects wrappers and functions.

name: isNullish
summary: Checks whether a value is `null` or `undefined`.
notes: Uses strict comparisons with `null` and `undefined`. The browser object `document.all` returns `false`, despite its historical loose equality with `null`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is `null` or `undefined`; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check for absent values while retaining `0`, `false` and the empty string. Unlike loose comparison with `null`, it does not treat the browser object `document.all` as absent.

name: isEmpty
summary: Checks whether a value is nullish or a supported string or container has no items.
notes:
Strings, genuine Maps and Sets, and validated array-like lengths are checked first. For other inputs, callable iterator methods or `next` take precedence over dictionary keys and cause `TypeError`. These methods are detected but never called. This also applies to plain dictionaries exposing those capabilities.

Remaining plain dictionaries are empty when they have no own enumerable string keys. Unsupported values, such as numbers or Dates, return `false`. Property getters and proxy traps can still run: avoiding iteration does not guarantee a check without side effects.

Use `isEmptyIterable` to consume a synchronous iterable. A `next`-only iterator needs an iterable adapter; asynchronous iteration must be handled by the caller. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is nullish or a supported string or container with no items; otherwise `false`.
description: Checks strings, arrays, array-like values, native Maps and Sets, and plain dictionaries without consuming an iterator. `null` and `undefined` count as empty; `[null]` does not. Unsized iterators and iterables throw because their contents cannot be checked without consumption.
tooltip: Uses lengths, collection sizes or dictionary keys. Unsized iterators and iterables throw `TypeError`; getters and proxy traps may run. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
errors: `TypeError` for unsized iterators or iterables. Property getters and proxy traps may throw. See [Empty and blank values](#empty-and-blank-values).

name: isBlank
summary: Checks whether a value is nullish, an empty or whitespace-only string, or a supported container containing only nullish values.
notes:
Uses the same input order and unsized-input errors as `isEmpty`. Map checks examine values, Set checks examine items, and dictionary checks examine own enumerable string-keyed values. Iterator capabilities take precedence over plain-dictionary handling.

The check is shallow: every inspected value must be `null` or `undefined`. Empty strings and empty objects inside a container are not nullish. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is nullish, a whitespace-only string, or a supported container containing only nullish values; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts nullish values, empty or whitespace-only strings, and supported containers whose contents are all `null` or `undefined`. The check is shallow: `[null]` is blank, but `[""]` is not. Unsized iterators and iterables throw instead of being consumed.
tooltip: Shallow and non-consuming. Map checks inspect values. Unsized iterators and iterables throw `TypeError`; getters and proxy traps may run. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
errors: `TypeError` for unsized iterators or iterables. Property getters and proxy traps may throw. See [Empty and blank values](#empty-and-blank-values).

name: isTruthy
summary: Checks whether JavaScript treats a value as `true` in a condition.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is truthy under JavaScript boolean coercion; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses ordinary boolean coercion: non-empty strings and objects are truthy, including `"false"`, `[]` and `new Boolean(false)`. It does not parse boolean text.

name: isFalsy
summary: Checks whether JavaScript treats a value as `false` in a condition.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is falsy under JavaScript boolean coercion; otherwise `false`.
description: Returns the opposite of `isTruthy`. This includes values such as `false`, `0`, `""`, `null`, `undefined` and `NaN`; it does not mean only absent values.

name: isInteger
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is an integer.
notes:
Reads genuine Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive or boxed finite integral number; otherwise `false`.
description: Finite whole numbers pass; fractional values, `NaN` and infinities do not. Genuine `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts genuine `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isSafeInteger
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is an integer in JavaScript’s safe-integer range.
notes:
Reads genuine Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive or boxed integer within the safe-integer range; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts integers from `-9007199254740991` through `9007199254740991`, inclusive. Genuine `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts genuine `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isFloat
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is a finite number with a fractional part.
notes:
Reads genuine Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive or boxed finite non-integer number; otherwise `false`.
description: A number such as `1.5` passes; whole numbers, `NaN` and infinities do not. Genuine `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts genuine `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isFinite
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is a finite number.
notes:
Reads genuine Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive or boxed finite number; otherwise `false`.
description: Rejects `NaN` and positive or negative infinity. Genuine `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts genuine `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isInfinite
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is positive or negative infinity.
notes:
Reads genuine Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is primitive or boxed positive or negative infinity; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts `Infinity` and `-Infinity`; finite numbers and `NaN` do not pass. Genuine `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts genuine `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isNaN
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is `NaN`.
notes:
Reads genuine Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is primitive or boxed `NaN`; otherwise `false`.
description: Detects the not-a-number value without converting strings or other inputs. Genuine `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts genuine `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isNumeric
summary: Checks whether a value is a finite number, a bigint, or non-blank numeric text.
notes: Uses standard numeric conversion syntax, not a decimal-only grammar. It rejects `NaN`, `Infinity`, empty/whitespace-only strings, boolean values, boxed `BigInt` values and arbitrary coercible objects. A passing string need not be exactly representable or within the safe-integer range; underflow to zero still passes.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a finite primitive or boxed number, a primitive bigint, or non-blank string text converting to a finite number; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check when numeric strings should be accepted without converting the caller’s value. Primitive and boxed finite numbers, primitive bigints, and primitive or boxed strings that convert to finite numbers pass. Empty or whitespace-only strings do not.
tooltip: Accepts numeric text as well as finite numbers and primitive bigints. Rejects booleans, blank text, `NaN`, infinities and boxed bigints.

name: isTypeOf
summary: Checks whether a value matches a type name, instance target, predicate or union of matchers.
notes:
The whole specification is validated before matching, including branches that evaluation would skip. Invalid names, descriptors, unions and non-callable instance hooks throw `TypeError`. No constructor body is invoked and no input conversion occurs.

Callable instance targets use native `instanceof`; an invalid target prototype can therefore throw during matching. An omitted `type` matches only `undefined`. By contrast, the string matcher `"undefined"` follows native `typeof` and also matches browser `document.all`. See [Type specifications](#type-specifications).
summaryReturn: `true` if the value matches the type specification (omission matches `undefined`); otherwise `false`.
description: Matches one value immediately, without converting it or invoking constructor bodies. Use a string such as `"number"` for a native `typeof` check, `{ predicate: fn }` for a custom check, or an array for alternatives.
tooltip: Validates the entire specification before matching. An omitted type matches `undefined`. Predicates must return a synchronous primitive boolean.
errors: Invalid matcher configuration throws `TypeError`. Callback, property-access and native instance-matching errors propagate; see [Type specifications](#type-specifications).

name: isObject
summary: Checks whether a value is a non-null object or function.
notes: Uses the JavaScript object/function boundary, so objects from another realm pass without needing a local `instanceof Object` match. The browser object `document.all` also passes despite its legacy `typeof` result.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a non-null object or function; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts objects of any supported shape, including arrays, dates, wrapper objects and functions. It does not require a plain dictionary or a particular prototype. `null` returns `false`.

name: isPlainObject
summary: Checks whether a value has a null or ordinary `Object` prototype.
notes: An own `constructor` field is ordinary data and is not read. Assigning `null` or `Object.prototype` as another object’s prototype can change the result. The browser object `document.all` follows this current-prototype rule too; its usual `HTMLAllCollection` prototype does not pass. This is a prototype classification, not a record of how the value was allocated or a validation of its fields.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value has a null or ordinary `Object` prototype; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises ordinary object literals and null-prototype dictionaries, including from another realm. Arrays and class instances with their usual prototypes do not pass. This classifies the current prototype; it does not prove how the value was created or validate its fields.
tooltip: Checks the current prototype, not allocation history or a schema. Proxy traps may run; an own `constructor` field is not read.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isCyclic
summary: Checks whether following enumerable string-keyed properties leads back to an ancestor.
notes:
A cycle must lead back to a value on the current traversal path; shared acyclic children do not count. Traversal is iterative, and completed shared nodes are visited once. Symbols, non-enumerable properties and Map/Set entries are ignored.

The graph is expected to remain stable during the check. Getters and proxy traps can mutate it or throw. Internal reference tracking falls back to local arrays when weak collections are unavailable; no platform globals are changed.
summaryReturn: `true` if enumerable string-keyed property traversal reaches an active ancestor; otherwise `false`.
description: Detects a cycle in an object graph, including through inherited enumerable properties. Two properties sharing the same acyclic child do not form a cycle. Getters and proxy traps may run as properties are inspected.
tooltip: Includes inherited enumerable string keys, but ignores symbols, non-enumerable properties and Map/Set entries. Getters and proxy traps may run. Internal reference tracking falls back to local arrays when weak collections are unavailable; no platform globals are changed.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isIterable
summary: Checks whether a value exposes a synchronous iterator method.
notes: The `Symbol.iterator` property is read, but its method is not called. A getter or proxy trap can run or throw, and a callable method can still return an invalid iterator.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value has a callable `Symbol.iterator` method; otherwise `false`.
description: Returns `true` when `Symbol.iterator` is callable. The method is not invoked, so this detects the capability without consuming the value or proving that iteration will work.
tooltip: Reads `Symbol.iterator` without calling it. Getters and proxy traps may run; method presence does not guarantee a valid iterator.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isArray
summary: Checks whether a value is an array, including from another realm.
notes: Uses the `Array.isArray` function captured when the module loads. This retains native behaviour for arrays from another realm and proxies, including `TypeError` for a revoked proxy.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value passes native `Array.isArray`; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses native `Array.isArray` behaviour. Arrays and non-revoked proxies around arrays pass; array-like objects do not. A revoked proxy throws.
tooltip: Preserves native `Array.isArray` behaviour, including `TypeError` for a revoked proxy.
errors: `TypeError` for a revoked proxy, following native `Array.isArray` behaviour.

name: isArrayOf
summary: Checks whether an array contains only values matching a type specification.
notes:
The length is read once; indexed values are read as matching proceeds. Missing positions read as `undefined` unless an inherited numeric property supplies a value. Appends beyond the original length are ignored.

Matcher validation happens before any container check. Invalid configuration throws for empty and non-collection inputs too; a valid empty container passes. An array exposing an invalid length, for example through a proxy, returns `false`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is an array and every element matches the specification, including an empty array; otherwise `false`.
description: Validates the entire matcher before checking the container, then checks each element until a mismatch is found. An empty container passes a valid matcher. Invalid configuration throws even when the input is empty or is not the expected container type.
tooltip: Validates the matcher before inspecting the input. Empty containers pass; evaluation stops at the first mismatch. Missing array positions read as `undefined` unless inherited numeric properties supply values.
errors: Invalid matcher configuration throws `TypeError`. Callback, property-access and native instance-matching errors propagate; see [Type specifications](#type-specifications).

name: isArrayLike
summary: Checks whether a non-function value has a valid numeric length.
notes: The `length` must already be a primitive number in the accepted range; boxed lengths, negative values, fractions, `NaN` and infinities are rejected. Missing indices are allowed. Reading `length` can invoke a getter or proxy trap.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is not a function and has a numeric integer length from `0` through `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts lengths that are integers from `0` through `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. It does not require an iterator or stored values at every index. The length is read once; getters and proxy traps may run.
tooltip: Reads `length` once. Missing indices are allowed; boxed, negative, fractional or non-finite lengths are rejected.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isArrayLikeOf
summary: Checks whether an array-like value contains only values matching a type specification.
notes:
The length is read once; indexed values are read as matching proceeds. Missing positions read as `undefined` unless an inherited numeric property supplies a value. Appends beyond the original length are ignored.

Matcher validation happens before any container check. Invalid configuration throws for empty and non-collection inputs too; a valid empty container passes.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is array-like and every indexed value matches the specification, including an empty input; otherwise `false`.
description: Validates the entire matcher before checking the container, then checks each indexed value until a mismatch is found. An empty container passes a valid matcher. Invalid configuration throws even when the input is empty or is not the expected container type.
tooltip: Validates the matcher before inspecting the input. Empty containers pass; evaluation stops at the first mismatch. Missing array positions read as `undefined` unless inherited numeric properties supply values.
errors: Invalid matcher configuration throws `TypeError`. Callback, property-access and native instance-matching errors propagate; see [Type specifications](#type-specifications).

name: isPair
summary: Checks whether a value is an array of length two.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is an array of length `2`; otherwise `false`.
description: Checks the array’s length rather than whether both positions contain values. Sparse arrays of length two pass; array-like objects do not.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate. Native `Array.isArray` also throws `TypeError` for a revoked proxy.

name: isMap
summary: Checks whether a value is a genuine `Map`.
notes: Uses native collection identity across realms without enumerating or changing the contents. A custom `Symbol.toStringTag` is ignored. A proxy or an object merely inheriting the collection prototype returns `false`. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `Map`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `Map` instances, including from another realm. It does not enumerate or modify the collection. Proxies, prototype imitations and matching tags do not establish native identity.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances without enumerating contents; rejects proxies and prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isSet
summary: Checks whether a value is a genuine `Set`.
notes: Uses native collection identity across realms without enumerating or changing the contents. A custom `Symbol.toStringTag` is ignored. A proxy or an object merely inheriting the collection prototype returns `false`. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `Set`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `Set` instances, including from another realm. It does not enumerate or modify the collection. Proxies, prototype imitations and matching tags do not establish native identity.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances without enumerating contents; rejects proxies and prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isWeakMap
summary: Checks whether a value is a genuine `WeakMap`.
notes: Uses native collection identity across realms without enumerating or changing the contents. A custom `Symbol.toStringTag` is ignored. A proxy or an object merely inheriting the collection prototype returns `false`. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `WeakMap`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `WeakMap` instances, including from another realm. It does not enumerate or modify the collection. Proxies, prototype imitations and matching tags do not establish native identity.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances without enumerating contents; rejects proxies and prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isWeakSet
summary: Checks whether a value is a genuine `WeakSet`.
notes: Uses native collection identity across realms without enumerating or changing the contents. A custom `Symbol.toStringTag` is ignored. A proxy or an object merely inheriting the collection prototype returns `false`. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `WeakSet`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `WeakSet` instances, including from another realm. It does not enumerate or modify the collection. Proxies, prototype imitations and matching tags do not establish native identity.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances without enumerating contents; rejects proxies and prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isFunction
summary: Checks whether JavaScript reports a value as a function.
notes: Classes, generators and callable proxies pass the native `typeof` check. A class still requires `new`, and a proxy or function can throw when called.
summaryReturn: `true` if `typeof value` is `"function"`; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses `typeof value === "function"`, which includes ordinary functions, classes, generators and callable proxies. Passing does not mean the value can be invoked without `new` or without throwing.
tooltip: Includes classes and callable proxies; does not guarantee a successful call.

name: isDate
summary: Checks whether a value is a genuine `Date`, valid or invalid.
notes: Uses a captured native Date operation across realms. Overridden instance `getTime` methods are ignored. The existence of a Date object and the validity of its timestamp are separate checks.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `Date`, valid or invalid; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native Date objects, including from another realm, without relying on their exposed `getTime` method. Use `isValidDate` when a usable timestamp is required.

name: isValidDate
summary: Checks whether a genuine `Date` contains a finite timestamp.
notes: Reads the timestamp through a captured native Date operation, ignoring overridden instance `getTime` methods. Dates from another realm are supported; non-Date values return `false`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `Date` with a finite timestamp; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this after constructing or converting a date when invalid dates must be rejected. Non-Date inputs return `false`; native Date objects from another realm are supported.

name: isInvalidDate
summary: Checks whether a genuine `Date` contains a `NaN` timestamp.
notes: Reads the timestamp through a captured native Date operation, ignoring overridden instance `getTime` methods. Dates from another realm are supported; non-Date values return `false`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `Date` with a `NaN` timestamp; otherwise `false`.
description: Detects an invalid Date object, such as `new Date("not a date")`. It does not classify non-Date values as invalid dates; those return `false`.

name: isRegExp
summary: Checks whether a value is a genuine regular-expression object.
notes: The browser fallback reads the native regular-expression source getter without executing the expression. Objects from another realm are supported; `RegExp.prototype`, proxies and prototype or tag imitations are rejected.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `RegExp` instance; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises `RegExp` instances, including from another realm, without executing the expression or changing `lastIndex`. Prototype or tag imitations do not pass.

name: isPromise
summary: Checks whether a value passes the local native `Promise` instance check.
notes: The local `Promise` constructor is checked at call time. A promise from another realm can fail, and an object inheriting `Promise.prototype` can pass. The check neither subscribes to a promise nor creates a derived promise. It returns `boolean` in TypeScript.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value passes the local native `Promise` instance check; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this for `instanceof Promise` behaviour in the current realm. A promise from another realm can return `false`, while an object inheriting `Promise.prototype` can return `true`. The check does not call `then` or subscribe to the promise.
tooltip: Uses local `instanceof` semantics; it is not proof of native Promise identity. Does not call `then`.
errors: Native `instanceof` errors propagate, including errors from proxy prototype access or a custom `Symbol.hasInstance` method.

name: isPromiseLike
summary: Checks whether a value is an object or function with callable `then` and `catch` methods.
notes: The library requires both `then` and `catch`. This is stricter than `isThenable` and differs from TypeScript’s `PromiseLike` interface. Neither method is invoked, but reading the properties can execute getters or proxy traps.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a non-null object or function with callable `then` and `catch` methods; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this for the library’s two-method Promise-like convention. Unlike `isThenable`, it requires both methods; unlike `isPromise`, it does not require a local native instance. Neither method is called.
tooltip: Requires both `then` and `catch`, unlike TypeScript `PromiseLike`. Does not invoke them; getters or proxy traps may run.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isThenable
summary: Checks whether a value is an object or function with a callable `then` method.
notes: Objects from another realm and null-prototype objects can pass. The `then` method is read but not invoked. Its presence does not prove compliance with the Promises/A+ rules.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a non-null object or function with a callable `then` method; otherwise `false`.
description: Detects the shape used by promise resolution, without invoking `then` or requiring a `catch` method. A passing result does not prove that the object follows Promise behaviour.
tooltip: Does not invoke `then` or prove Promise behaviour. Getters and proxy traps may run.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isError
summary: Checks whether a value is recognised as an error by the available native check or fallback.
notes: When `Error.isError` is unavailable, the fallback refuses an own or inherited `Symbol.toStringTag` without reading its getter. If the tag key is also unavailable, it returns `false` without inspecting the object rather than trusting a possibly customised tag. Genuine errors can therefore fail when detection capabilities are missing. When available, the captured native check determines the result. Proxy traps can still run when the fallback has a usable tag key; the result is not a security guarantee.
summaryReturn: `true` if the captured native error check, or its conservative fallback, recognises the value as an error; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses the captured `Error.isError` function when the host provides it. Otherwise, it recognises ordinary untagged Error objects conservatively and rejects custom tags without reading the tag getter. The fallback returns `false` if `Symbol.toStringTag` is unavailable, including for genuine errors.
tooltip: The fallback rejects custom tags without reading their getters. Without native branding or a usable tag key, returns `false`. Proxy traps may run; this is not a security check.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isNode
summary: Checks whether a value is an instance of the local DOM `Node` constructor.
notes: Positive examples require a browser with the corresponding DOM constructor. The constructor is checked at call time; absence produces `false`. Native local-instance rules apply, so this does not validate an object’s properties or recognise every DOM object from another realm.
summaryReturn: `true` if a local `Node` constructor is available and the value passes its instance check; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this for DOM objects from the current browser realm. Returns `false` when the constructor is unavailable; objects from an iframe or another realm may fail the local instance check.
tooltip: Returns `false` when the local constructor is unavailable. Does not recognise all foreign-realm DOM objects.
errors: Native `instanceof` errors propagate, including errors from proxy prototype access or a custom `Symbol.hasInstance` method.

name: isElement
summary: Checks whether a value is an instance of the local DOM `Element` constructor.
notes: Positive examples require a browser with the corresponding DOM constructor. The constructor is checked at call time; absence produces `false`. Native local-instance rules apply, so this does not validate an object’s properties or recognise every DOM object from another realm.
summaryReturn: `true` if a local `Element` constructor is available and the value passes its instance check; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this for DOM objects from the current browser realm. Returns `false` when the constructor is unavailable; objects from an iframe or another realm may fail the local instance check.
tooltip: Returns `false` when the local constructor is unavailable. Does not recognise all foreign-realm DOM objects.
errors: Native `instanceof` errors propagate, including errors from proxy prototype access or a custom `Symbol.hasInstance` method.

name: isFragment
summary: Checks whether a value is an instance of the local DOM `DocumentFragment` constructor.
notes: Positive examples require a browser with the corresponding DOM constructor. The constructor is checked at call time; absence produces `false`. Native local-instance rules apply, so this does not validate an object’s properties or recognise every DOM object from another realm.
summaryReturn: `true` if a local `DocumentFragment` constructor is available and the value passes its instance check; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this for DOM objects from the current browser realm. Returns `false` when the constructor is unavailable; objects from an iframe or another realm may fail the local instance check.
tooltip: Returns `false` when the local constructor is unavailable. Does not recognise all foreign-realm DOM objects.
errors: Native `instanceof` errors propagate, including errors from proxy prototype access or a custom `Symbol.hasInstance` method.

name: isArrayBuffer
summary: Checks whether a value is a genuine `ArrayBuffer`.
notes: Custom tags are ignored. A detached ArrayBuffer retains its native identity; use the intended buffer operation to determine whether memory is usable. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `ArrayBuffer`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native ArrayBuffer objects, including from another realm. Proxies and prototype or tag imitations do not pass. A detached buffer still passes: this check does not establish that its memory can be used.
tooltip: Checks identity rather than memory usability; supports foreign instances and rejects proxies. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isSharedArrayBuffer
summary: Checks whether a value is a genuine `SharedArrayBuffer`.
notes: Custom tags are ignored. This identifies a shared buffer; it does not validate the memory access or synchronisation required by the caller. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if native shared buffers are available and the value is a genuine `SharedArrayBuffer`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native shared buffers, including from another realm, without accepting proxies or prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the host does not provide `SharedArrayBuffer`.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances and rejects proxies or prototype imitations. Returns `false` when native shared buffers are unavailable. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isArrayBufferView
summary: Checks whether a value is a native typed array or `DataView`.
notes: Native view identity survives detachment. Proxies and objects that merely inherit a view prototype are rejected. A passing result does not guarantee that a later memory operation will succeed. Falls back to native DataView and typed-array identity checks when `ArrayBuffer.isView` is unavailable; returns `false` if none of those checks is available.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a native typed array or `DataView`; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses native `ArrayBuffer.isView` to recognise views, including detached views and views from another realm. Ordinary arrays, proxies and prototype imitations return `false`.
tooltip: Detached views retain their identity; passing does not guarantee usable memory. Falls back to native DataView and typed-array identity checks when `ArrayBuffer.isView` is unavailable; returns `false` if none of those checks is available.

name: isTypedArray
summary: Checks whether a value is a native typed array, including a Node.js `Buffer`.
notes:
Includes subclasses, foreign instances, Node.js Buffers and detached or out-of-bounds views. Uses native view identity and the built-in typed-array tag getter rather than an exposed custom tag.

The declaration describes the common typed-array surface; it does not identify the element type or guarantee usable memory. Uses captured native tag or length getters; returns `false` if no usable native detection getter is available. Missing `Symbol`, `Reflect` or `ArrayBuffer.isView` does not prevent loading.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a native typed array, including a Node.js `Buffer`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts number and bigint typed arrays, subclasses and foreign instances. Ordinary arrays and `DataView` objects are excluded. Detached or out-of-bounds views still pass because this checks identity, not memory usability.
tooltip: Excludes `DataView` and ordinary arrays; detached views still pass. Does not identify a particular element type. Uses captured native tag or length getters; returns `false` if no usable native detection getter is available. Missing `Symbol`, `Reflect` or `ArrayBuffer.isView` does not prevent loading.

name: isDataView
summary: Checks whether a value is a genuine `DataView`.
notes: Custom tags are ignored; proxies and prototype imitations return `false`. Detached and out-of-bounds views retain their identity, so a passing result does not guarantee that a later memory operation will succeed. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a genuine `DataView`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `DataView` identity, including from another realm, without accepting proxies or prototype/tag imitations. Identity does not guarantee usable memory: detached or out-of-bounds objects retain their identity.
tooltip: Checks identity rather than memory usability; supports foreign instances and rejects proxies. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isAsyncIterable
summary: Checks whether a value exposes an asynchronous iterator method.
notes:
Checks the explicit `Symbol.asyncIterator` protocol. A synchronous iterable does not pass solely because `for await...of` could adapt it. A callable method need not return a valid iterator.

When `Symbol.asyncIterator` is unavailable, the result is `false` and the input is not inspected. Returns `false` without inspecting the input when `Symbol` itself or `Symbol.asyncIterator` is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the async-iterator symbol is available and the value has a callable `Symbol.asyncIterator` method; otherwise `false`.
description: Returns `true` when `Symbol.asyncIterator` is available and callable on the value. It does not invoke the method, and a synchronous-only iterable does not pass just because `for await...of` could adapt it.
tooltip: Does not invoke the method. Returns `false` without inspecting the value when `Symbol.asyncIterator` is unavailable. Returns `false` without inspecting the input when `Symbol` itself or `Symbol.asyncIterator` is unavailable.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isIteratorLike
summary: Checks whether a value is an object or function with a callable `next` method.
notes: Reads `next` without calling it. This cannot distinguish synchronous from asynchronous iteration or guarantee a valid `IteratorResult` object.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a non-null object or function with a callable `next` method; otherwise `false`.
description: Detects the shape of an iterator without advancing it. The method may be synchronous or asynchronous; this check does not validate the values returned by `next`.
tooltip: Does not invoke `next` or validate iterator results. Property getters and proxy traps may run.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isNonNullish
summary: Checks whether a value is neither `null` nor `undefined`.
notes: The generic declaration narrows to `NonNullable<T>`. Values such as `0`, `false`, `""`, `NaN` and `0n` are retained.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is neither `null` nor `undefined`; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check to retain present values, including `0`, `false` and the empty string. It can be passed to `Array.filter` and narrows the TypeScript result to `NonNullable<T>`.

name: isObjectLike
summary: Checks whether a value is a non-null object, excluding functions.
notes: Includes browser `document.all`, but does not require a plain dictionary. The declaration returns `boolean` because TypeScript’s `object` type also includes functions.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a non-null object other than a function; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check when functions should be excluded from the object category. Arrays, dates and wrapper objects still pass; use `isPlainObject` for plain dictionaries.

name: isNonEmptyArray
summary: Checks whether a value is an array with a valid length greater than zero.
notes: A hole contributes to array length without storing a value. Element types are not checked. An invalid exposed array length, for example through a proxy, returns `false`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is an array with a valid length greater than zero; otherwise `false`.
description: Checks array identity and length without validating the elements. A hole contributes to length, so `Array(1)` is non-empty even though it has no stored element.
tooltip: Sparse arrays count as non-empty when their length is positive. Does not validate elements.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate. Native `Array.isArray` also throws `TypeError` for a revoked proxy.

name: isJson
summary: Checks whether primitive or boxed string text is valid JSON.
notes: Uses the captured `JSON.parse` function and ignores boxed-string conversion overrides. JSON scalar text passes as well as object or array text. Parse errors produce `false`; no parsed value is retained for the caller. Syntax validity does not enforce unique object keys, finite numeric results or lossless numeric parsing.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is primitive or boxed string text that parses as JSON; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts text representing JSON objects, arrays or scalar values such as `"42"` and `"null"`. It does not return the parsed value, check a schema, or test whether an arbitrary object can be serialised. Use `fromJson` when you need the parsed result.
tooltip: Accepts text representing JSON objects, arrays or scalar values. Does not validate a schema or arbitrary-object serialisability.

name: isSetOf
summary: Checks whether a Set contains only values matching a type specification.
notes:
Uses captured native Set iteration, ignoring an overridden iterator method. Iteration is live: predicates must not mutate the Set because mutation can change the result or prevent termination.

The matcher is validated even for an empty or non-Set input. An empty Set passes a valid matcher. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `Set` whose items all match the specification, including an empty `Set`; otherwise `false`.
description: Validates the entire matcher before checking the container, then checks each item until a mismatch is found. An empty container passes a valid matcher. Invalid configuration throws even when the input is empty or is not the expected container type.
tooltip: Validates the matcher before inspecting the input. Empty containers pass; evaluation stops at the first mismatch. Predicates must not mutate the Set. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
errors: Invalid matcher configuration throws `TypeError`. Callback, property-access and native instance-matching errors propagate; see [Type specifications](#type-specifications).

name: isMapOf
summary: Checks whether every Map key and value matches its respective specification.
notes:
Uses captured native Map entry iteration, ignoring an overridden iterator method and supporting Maps from another realm. Evaluation stops at the first failed key or value. Iteration is live: predicates must not mutate the Map.

Both matchers are validated even for an empty or non-Map input. An empty Map passes valid matchers. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `Map` whose keys and values match their respective specifications, including an empty `Map`; otherwise `false`.
description: Validates both matchers before inspecting the input, then checks each key before its associated value. An empty Map passes valid matchers. Native Map iteration is live, so predicates must not mutate the Map.
tooltip: Validates both matchers first; empty Maps pass. Checks each key before its value. Predicates must not mutate the Map. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
errors: Invalid matcher configuration throws `TypeError`. Callback, property-access and native instance-matching errors propagate; see [Type specifications](#type-specifications).

name: isEmptyIterable
summary: Checks whether a synchronous iterable is empty by advancing its iterator.
notes: A non-iterable input throws `TypeError`. Finding an item produces an early `false` and closes the iterator using native `for...of` rules. Closing can call `return()` or run generator `finally` blocks. Do not reuse a one-shot iterator after inspection.
summaryReturn: `true` if the synchronous iterable yields no items; otherwise `false`.
description: Advances the iterable until the first item or completion. An item produces `false` and closes the iterator early; completion without an item produces `true`. This can consume or close a one-shot iterator, so do not reuse it after inspection.
tooltip: Consumes input and may close it early, running iterator cleanup. Requires a synchronous iterable; do not reuse one-shot input.
errors: `TypeError` for non-iterable input. Iterator and iterator-closing errors propagate.

name: isBlankIterable
summary: Checks whether every item yielded by a synchronous iterable is nullish by advancing its iterator.
notes:
Checks yielded items themselves. A non-empty Map yields entry arrays, so it returns `false` even when every Map value is nullish; `isBlank(map)` instead checks the Map’s values.

Finding a non-nullish item closes the iterator early, which can run cleanup code. Iteration and closing errors propagate. A nullish-only infinite iterable never completes.
summaryReturn: `true` if the synchronous iterable yields no items or only nullish items; otherwise `false`.
description: Returns `true` for an empty iterable or one yielding only `null` and `undefined`. Stops and closes the iterator at the first other item. The check is shallow and can consume or close one-shot input.
tooltip: Consumes input and may close it early. A nullish-only infinite iterable never completes. Map entries are arrays, so a non-empty Map is not blank.
errors: `TypeError` for non-iterable input. Iterator and iterator-closing errors propagate.

name: toArray
summary: Converts a synchronous iterable, plain record or supported array-like input to a new shallow array.
notes:
Functions, boxed primitives, Dates and RegExps are rejected before inspecting iterator or length properties. Other non-string primitives are unsupported. On eligible inputs a synchronous iterator takes precedence over record properties and indexed values. The iterator method is read once and called with the original input as receiver; null or undefined permits fallback, while other non-callable methods throw.

Plain records include null-prototype and foreign-realm records. Own string and symbol keys are snapshotted in property order; each current enumerable descriptor is checked and each included value is read once. Inherited and non-enumerable properties are excluded, newly added keys are not copied, and deleted or newly hidden keys are skipped. A length property is ordinary record data.

Only non-plain array-like inputs use indexed fallback. Their length must be a primitive number that is an integer between zero and Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, matching isArrayLike; strings, fractions and coercible objects are rejected. Length is read once and indexed values are read live. Missing slots become explicit undefined and inherited numeric values are included. Strings iterate by Unicode code point. Nested values retain identity.

Ordinary promises and native async-only containers without a supported synchronous source are rejected. No input is awaited. A plain async-only record is copied as data, including an enumerable async-iterator symbol and its value. Finite one-shot iterators are consumed; infinite iterables do not finish and very large inputs can exhaust memory. Requires native Array.from. Record copying requires Reflect.ownKeys or Object.getOwnPropertySymbols; if both are missing it throws instead of silently discarding possible symbol keys.

If a copied record has an enumerable nullish Symbol.iterator value, the value captured during source dispatch is reused; its getter is not read a second time. Other selected property values are read live after checking their current descriptor.
summaryReturn: A new shallow array containing iterable items, own enumerable record values or indexed array-like values.
description: Consumes synchronous iterables first, copies plain-record values second, and reads supported non-plain array-like inputs third. Record values include own enumerable string and symbol properties, including a property named length. Nullish input and unsupported values throw instead of producing an empty array.
tooltip: Consumes iterable input, copies own enumerable string and symbol record values, or reads supported array-like indices. Array-like lengths must already be numeric safe integers at least zero. Nullish and unsupported inputs throw. Requires native `Array.from`; missing support throws `TypeError` before inspecting the input.
errors: TypeError for nullish or unsupported input, malformed iterators or invalid array-like lengths. Oversized array results can throw RangeError. Getter, proxy and iterator errors propagate. Missing native Array.from throws before conversion; record copying requires symbol-enumeration support.

name: toArrayIf
summary: Converts supported iterable, record or array-like input to a new shallow array when the condition evaluates to `true`. Otherwise, returns the original value unchanged.
notes:
A predicate receives the original value once, without an explicit `this` receiver. It must return a primitive boolean; other results, including Promises, throw `TypeError`. Promise results are not awaited and no rejection handler is attached.

Predicate errors propagate. A predicate can mutate its input; a requested conversion then sees that mutation. No clone or rollback is introduced. A skipped conversion does not inspect the input. When requested, conversion follows the full `toArray` contract.
summaryReturn: A new shallow array when conversion is requested; otherwise the original input, unchanged.
description: Uses the same conversion as `toArray` when requested. A primitive boolean is used directly; a predicate receives the original input once and must return a primitive boolean. A `false`, omitted or `undefined` condition returns the input unchanged without inspecting or converting it.
tooltip: Calls a predicate once. A skipped conversion preserves the input without inspection. Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`.
errors: Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`. Predicate errors propagate. A requested conversion also follows [`toArray`](#toarrayvalue) error behaviour; a skipped conversion does not inspect or coerce the value.

name: toBigInt
summary: Converts a value to a primitive bigint using native conversion.
notes:
Empty and whitespace-only strings become `0n`. Fractional or non-finite numbers throw `RangeError`; invalid integer text throws `SyntaxError`; `null`, `undefined` and symbols throw `TypeError`. Number inputs may already have lost precision before conversion.

Native BigInt support requires Node.js 10.4 or later. Without it, this operation throws `TypeError` before coercing the input. Importing the package and using other functions still works.
summaryReturn: The converted primitive bigint.
description: Accepts booleans, integral numbers and integer text, including hexadecimal, binary and octal forms. Use bigint or integer text when exactness matters: conversion cannot recover precision already lost in a Number. Native BigInt support is required only when this conversion is called.
tooltip: Requires native BigInt. Fractional numbers and invalid integer text throw; input conversion hooks may run.
errors: `RangeError` for fractional or non-finite numbers; `SyntaxError` for invalid integer text; `TypeError` for nullish values, symbols, or unavailable native BigInt support. Object-coercion errors propagate.

name: toBigIntIf
summary: Converts a value to a primitive bigint when the condition evaluates to `true`. Otherwise, returns the original value unchanged.
notes:
A predicate receives the original value once, without an explicit `this` receiver. It must return a primitive boolean; other results, including Promises, throw `TypeError`. Promise results are not awaited and no rejection handler is attached.

Predicate errors propagate. A predicate can mutate its input; a requested conversion then sees that mutation. No clone or rollback is introduced. A skipped conversion does not inspect the input. When requested, conversion follows the full `toBigInt` contract. Skipping also works when native BigInt support is unavailable.
summaryReturn: The converted primitive bigint when conversion is requested; otherwise the original input, unchanged.
description: Uses the same conversion as `toBigInt` when requested. A primitive boolean is used directly; a predicate receives the original input once and must return a primitive boolean. A `false`, omitted or `undefined` condition returns the input unchanged without inspecting or converting it.
tooltip: Calls a predicate once. A skipped conversion preserves the input without inspection. Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`. Only a requested conversion requires native BigInt.
errors: Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`. Predicate errors propagate. A requested conversion also follows [`toBigInt`](#tobigintvalue) error behaviour; a skipped conversion does not inspect or coerce the value.

name: toBoolean
summary: Converts a value to a boolean using JavaScript truthiness.
notes:
Non-empty strings such as `"false"` and `"0"`, arrays and boxed `false` values are truthy. Objects are not unboxed and their conversion hooks are not called. The browser object `document.all` retains its platform-defined falsy behaviour.

For deliberate text parsing, use a separate parser such as go-booleans parseBool. Boolean parsing is not part of this helper and go-types does not add a runtime dependency on that package.
summaryReturn: `true` if the input is truthy under JavaScript boolean coercion; otherwise `false`.
description: Returns the input’s JavaScript truthiness. It does not parse text: `"false"`, `"0"`, arrays and boxed `false` values are truthy. Object conversion hooks are not called.
tooltip: Uses truthiness rather than parsing boolean text. Does not invoke object conversion hooks.

name: toBooleanIf
summary: Converts a value to its JavaScript boolean truthiness when the condition evaluates to `true`. Otherwise, returns the original value unchanged.
notes:
A predicate receives the original value once, without an explicit `this` receiver. It must return a primitive boolean; other results, including Promises, throw `TypeError`. Promise results are not awaited and no rejection handler is attached.

Predicate errors propagate. A predicate can mutate its input; a requested conversion then sees that mutation. No clone or rollback is introduced. A skipped conversion does not inspect the input. When requested, conversion follows the full `toBoolean` contract.
summaryReturn: The input’s boolean truthiness when conversion is requested; otherwise the original input, unchanged.
description: Uses the same conversion as `toBoolean` when requested. A primitive boolean is used directly; a predicate receives the original input once and must return a primitive boolean. A `false`, omitted or `undefined` condition returns the input unchanged without inspecting or converting it.
tooltip: Calls a predicate once. A skipped conversion preserves the input without inspection. Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`.
errors: Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`. Predicate errors propagate. A requested conversion also follows [`toBoolean`](#tobooleanvalue) error behaviour; a skipped conversion does not inspect or coerce the value.

name: toDate
summary: Converts a value to a `Date`, returning genuine `Date` objects unchanged. The result can be invalid.
notes:
Genuine Dates from any realm, subclasses and invalid Dates are returned unchanged. For other inputs, `new Date(value)` treats numbers as millisecond timestamps and strings as date text. Invalid text can produce an invalid Date; symbols, bigints and failed coercions can throw. Omitted or `undefined` input produces an invalid Date rather than the current time.

Prefer ISO date-time strings with an explicit timezone for portable string input. Standard date-only strings use UTC, while date-time strings without a timezone use local time; non-ISO parsing is runtime-dependent. Validate with `isValidDate` when needed. The TypeScript result is `Date`, not the input subtype: a structurally compatible input can require a new Date that lacks the input’s extra properties.

examples.expression: (() => { const date = new Date(0); return toDate(date) === date; })()

summaryReturn: The original genuine `Date`, or a new `Date` constructed from the input; it may be invalid.
description: Genuine Date objects retain their identity, including invalid dates and dates from another realm. Other inputs use `new Date(value)`. Invalid text and omitted input can produce an invalid Date; use `isValidDate` when a valid timestamp is required.
tooltip: Preserves genuine Date identity. May return an invalid Date; omitted input does not mean the current time. Symbols, bigints and conversion hooks can throw.
errors: Symbols, bigints and failed object coercion can throw. Invalid date text can instead produce an invalid `Date`; check with [`isValidDate`](#isvaliddatevalue).

name: toDateIf
summary: Converts a value to a `Date` when the condition evaluates to `true`. Otherwise, returns the original value unchanged.
notes:
A predicate receives the original value once, without an explicit `this` receiver. It must return a primitive boolean; other results, including Promises, throw `TypeError`. Promise results are not awaited and no rejection handler is attached.

Predicate errors propagate. A predicate can mutate its input; a requested conversion then sees that mutation. No clone or rollback is introduced. A skipped conversion does not inspect the input. When requested, conversion follows the full `toDate` contract.
summaryReturn: The original genuine `Date` or a new `Date`, possibly invalid, when conversion is requested; otherwise the original input, unchanged.
description: Uses the same conversion as `toDate` when requested. A primitive boolean is used directly; a predicate receives the original input once and must return a primitive boolean. A `false`, omitted or `undefined` condition returns the input unchanged without inspecting or converting it.
tooltip: Calls a predicate once. A skipped conversion preserves the input without inspection. Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`.
errors: Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`. Predicate errors propagate. A requested conversion also follows [`toDate`](#todatevalue) error behaviour; a skipped conversion does not inspect or coerce the value.

name: toInteger
summary: Converts a value to a number and truncates it towards zero.
notes:
Converts the whole value, so `"12px"` becomes `NaN` rather than `12`. Negative fractions truncate towards zero, unlike `Math.floor`. `NaN`, infinities and signed zero follow `Math.trunc` behaviour.

Number rounding, overflow and underflow happen before truncation. The operation does not clamp values or substitute defaults. Use `isInteger` or `isSafeInteger` to validate the result. Symbols and failing object conversions can throw.
summaryReturn: The numeric conversion truncated towards zero; it may be `NaN` or infinite.
description: Uses `Number` followed by `Math.trunc`, so `"12px"` becomes `NaN` rather than `12`. Negative fractions move towards zero. The result can still be `NaN`, infinite or outside the safe-integer range.
tooltip: Does not guarantee a finite or safe integer. Symbols and failing conversion hooks can throw.
errors: Symbols and failed object conversions can throw. `NaN` and infinity are returned rather than rejected.

name: toIntegerIf
summary: Converts a value to a number and truncates it towards zero when the condition evaluates to `true`. Otherwise, returns the original value unchanged.
notes:
A predicate receives the original value once, without an explicit `this` receiver. It must return a primitive boolean; other results, including Promises, throw `TypeError`. Promise results are not awaited and no rejection handler is attached.

Predicate errors propagate. A predicate can mutate its input; a requested conversion then sees that mutation. No clone or rollback is introduced. A skipped conversion does not inspect the input. When requested, conversion follows the full `toInteger` contract.
summaryReturn: The numeric conversion truncated towards zero, possibly `NaN` or infinite, when conversion is requested; otherwise the original input, unchanged.
description: Uses the same conversion as `toInteger` when requested. A primitive boolean is used directly; a predicate receives the original input once and must return a primitive boolean. A `false`, omitted or `undefined` condition returns the input unchanged without inspecting or converting it.
tooltip: Calls a predicate once. A skipped conversion preserves the input without inspection. Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`.
errors: Invalid conditions or non-boolean predicate results throw `TypeError`. Predicate errors propagate. A requested conversion also follows [`toInteger`](#tointegervalue) error behaviour; a skipped conversion does not inspect or coerce the value.

name: toJson
summary: Serialises a value to JSON text using native `JSON.stringify` behaviour.
description: Produces JSON text from objects, arrays and scalar values. Strings are encoded as JSON strings, even when they already contain JSON text. Accepts a native replacer callback or property-name list and optional indentation.
summaryReturn: JSON text, or `undefined` when native serialisation produces no text, including omitted input without a replacer.
tooltip: May return `undefined`. Does not transform Maps, Sets or bigints automatically. Cycles and unhandled bigints throw; getters, `toJSON` methods and replacer callbacks can run.
notes:
Without a replacer, top-level `undefined`, functions and symbols produce `undefined`; corresponding object properties are omitted and array positions become `null`. Non-finite numbers become `null`. Native `toJSON` methods apply, including Date serialisation. Ordinary Maps and Sets produce `{}` unless their own properties or custom hooks provide content.

A replacer callback receives `(key, value)` with the containing object as `this`, including a root call with key `""`. It runs after `toJSON` and may replace the root, omit properties or handle bigints. A replacer array selects string/number property names, including at nested object levels; duplicates are ignored. Other replacer-array elements are ignored except boxed strings/numbers, which native serialisation accepts. The `space` argument controls indentation, capped at ten spaces or ten string code units; non-whitespace indentation can produce text that is not valid JSON.

Native errors propagate unchanged. Shared references are allowed; circular traversal throws. Hooks may mutate input or throw, and no input or hook result is awaited. No cycle marker, Map/Set encoding, bigint representation or global polyfill is introduced. Exact escaping follows the host JSON implementation; output is not an HTML-safe escaping or canonicalisation service.
errors: Cycles and unhandled bigints throw `TypeError`. Getter, proxy, `toJSON` and replacer exceptions propagate unchanged.

examples.expression: toJson({a: 1, secret: 2}, (key, value) => key === 'secret' ? undefined : value)

name: toMap
summary: Converts a plain record or synchronous iterable of strict key/value pairs to a new shallow Map.
summaryReturn: A new Map containing own enumerable string and symbol record entries or strict iterable pairs, or an empty Map for omitted or nullish input.

Functions, boxed primitives, Dates and RegExps are rejected before iterator inspection. Plain records include null-prototype and foreign-realm records. Own string and symbol keys are captured once in property order; each current descriptor is checked before its enumerable value is read once. Inherited and non-enumerable properties are excluded, deleted or newly hidden keys are skipped, newly added keys are excluded, and nested values retain identity. Numeric property names become string keys; symbol keys stay symbols. An own constructor or length field is ordinary data.

A synchronous iterator takes precedence over record properties on eligible inputs. Its method is read once and called with the original input as receiver. A null or undefined iterator permits record conversion; other non-callable methods throw. Async iterators are never invoked or awaited. Each iterable entry must be an actual array of length exactly two, with own properties at both indices 0 and 1. Explicit undefined keys and values are valid. Holes, inherited-only indices, extra elements, strings and array-like entry objects are rejected. Any key type is allowed, without string coercion. Non-empty strings yield primitive entries and throw; an empty string yields no entries. There is no array-like source fallback.

Native SameValueZero key equality merges repeated NaN keys and treats negative and positive zero as the same key. The last value for a repeated key wins without moving its insertion position. Entry validation and property-access errors inside the loop close the outer iterator; the original error wins over a cleanup error. Native for-of failures while reading next, done or value propagate without an additional close attempt.

Finite one-shot iterators are consumed once; infinite inputs do not finish and no work limit is imposed. Requires native Map. Record copying requires Reflect.ownKeys or Object.getOwnPropertySymbols; missing both throws instead of dropping possible symbol keys.

notes:

name: toPlainObject
summary: Converts JSON object text, a plain object, or entry pairs into a fresh plain object.
notes:
Primitive JSON text must contain a non-null, non-array object; nested arrays are allowed. Boxed strings are not parsed. Other primitives, functions, Dates, RegExps and non-iterable class instances are unsupported. No primitive boxing, repairs or schema validation is performed.

A synchronous iterator takes precedence over copying record properties. Each entry must be an actual two-element array with both own slots present; an explicit undefined value is allowed. Extra or missing elements, strings and array-like entry objects are rejected. Duplicate keys use the last value. Keys are primitive strings or symbols and are never coerced. Special names such as __proto__, constructor, prototype and toString become ordinary own data properties.

Record copying snapshots own keys, checks each current enumerable descriptor and reads each included value once. Inherited and non-enumerable properties are omitted. Getters may mutate the source or throw. Results have writable, enumerable, configurable data properties and preserve nested references. TypeScript makes inferred properties optional because enumerability and presence cannot be proved structurally; JSON results contain unknown values. Prototype-name properties and broad string-key records also have unknown values because an omitted own key can expose an inherited property.

Consumes a synchronous iterable once; infinite inputs do not finish. Entry validation or property access in the loop closes the outer iterator, running return/finally cleanup. The original conversion error takes precedence over a cleanup error. Native for-of protocol failures in next, done or value propagate without an additional close attempt. Async iteration is never consumed or awaited. Async generators are unsupported; a plain async-only object is copied as a record, including enumerable symbol properties. Symbol enumeration requires Reflect.ownKeys or Object.getOwnPropertySymbols when copying records; missing both throws rather than silently discarding symbol keys. JSON and array-entry conversion remain available.

If a copied record has an enumerable nullish Symbol.iterator value, the value captured during source dispatch is reused; its getter is not read a second time. Other selected property values are read live after checking their current descriptor.
summaryReturn: A fresh ordinary object containing the parsed properties, copied enumerable properties, or supplied entries.
description: Parses primitive JSON object strings, shallow-copies plain records, or consumes synchronous entries. Every result has the local Object.prototype. Nullish input and unsupported values throw instead of being boxed.
tooltip: Returns a fresh ordinary object. Copies own enumerable string and symbol properties, preserving nested references. Entry pairs must be two-element arrays with string or symbol keys. Nullish input throws.

summaryReturn: A new Set of iterable items, own enumerable record values or indexed array-like values, or an empty Set for omitted or nullish input.

A synchronous iterator takes precedence over record and indexed data. Its method is read once and called with the original input as receiver; null or undefined permits fallback, while other non-callable methods throw.

name: fromJson
summary: Parses JSON text into a JavaScript value using native `JSON.parse` behaviour.
description: Parses JSON text representing objects, arrays or scalar values. An optional native reviver can transform or delete parsed values, including replacing the root.
summaryReturn: The parsed value, or any root value returned by the reviver, including `undefined`. TypeScript returns unknown until the caller validates it.
tooltip: Uses captured native `JSON.parse`, including input coercion, reviver order and errors. Parsing does not validate an application schema; reviver results are not awaited.
notes:
Native input coercion happens once before parsing; non-string inputs such as numbers, booleans and `null` follow `JSON.parse` rules. Omitted or `undefined` input and invalid JSON throw `SyntaxError`; symbol input throws `TypeError`. Nested strings that contain JSON text remain strings. Duplicate object names use the last value, and JSON numbers follow native `Number` precision and range.

A reviver is called for children before parents, then for the root with key "". Its this value is the containing object. Returning `undefined` deletes an object property, leaves an array hole or replaces the root with `undefined`. Other return values are retained as-is, including promises. Non-callable revivers are ignored by the native parser. Newer hosts may pass `source` context as a third argument; older supported runtimes do not. Both the context and its `source` property are optional in the declarations.

Native parsing creates own data properties for names such as `__proto__`; no property-copying or prototype assignment is added. Revivers may deliberately mutate their holder, return arbitrary objects or throw. JSON input coercion and reviver errors propagate unchanged. No automatic `Date`/`Map`/`Set` revival, JSON5 parsing, fallback value or generic type assertion is introduced.
